help.components:
rdc2blendCppCli components [options]

Lists the component modules that can be loaded - one per game - with
their id, label, ABI and the stages each implements.  Loads each DLL to
ask it, and changes nothing on disk.

  --component-file FILE  load this module as well, by path
  --list            one id per line, for a script
  --json            full detail as JSON

Which module a RUN uses is `run`'s --component/--tag, not this command's:
`components` reports what is on the search path, and asks no further.
help.doctor:
rdc2blendCppCli doctor [options]

Says where the tool thinks it is and what it found there: the tool root,
the component and env directories, the driver script, the Blender bridge,
the language file, the workspace, the component search path and
RenderDoc.  Reads and changes nothing, and needs neither a workspace nor
a working install - it is what to run when one of those is the thing
that is wrong.

  --root DIR         report on this tool root (default: the exe's own
                     directory)
  --workspace DIR    report on this workspace
  --json             the whole report as one JSON document

Exit code 2 means no component could be loaded: there is nothing to run.
help.emit_fbx:
rdc2blendCppCli emit-fbx [DIR] [options]

Writes each solved part out as a binary FBX.  Reads the meshes and the
manifest under world2/; DIR defaults to <workspace>/imi/<task>/solve.

  --work DIR         the directory holding world2/manifest.json
  --out DIR          where the .fbx files go (default <DIR>/fbx)
  --placement NAME   local | world.  `local` leaves each part as its own
                     geometry and writes no placement; `world` bakes the
                     recorded placement into the vertices
  --json             result as one JSON document on stdout
help.emit_scene:
rdc2blendCppCli emit-scene [DIR] [options]

Writes the neutral description file a DCC reads: the scene the parts go
into, the frame it is expressed in, and the camera.  Reads the manifest
under world2/; DIR defaults to <workspace>/imi/<task>/solve.

  --work DIR         the directory holding world2/manifest.json
  --out FILE|DIR     the description file (default <DIR>/scene<ext>)
  --ext EXT          its extension (default .rdc2scene)
  --geometry DIR     the directory the part files live in (default: the
                     manifest's own world directory)
  --geometry-ext EXT their extension - `.fbx` for FBX parts, the default
                     for meshes.  This is NOT --ext: naming the wrong one
                     is not an error, it points at files that are not
                     there
  --origin WHERE     world | character (default world).  `character` puts
                     the character's own local origin - the point its
                     placements share - at the scene's origin, and records
                     that point so a consumer moves everything, camera
                     included, by the same amount
  --no-camera        do not carry the recovered camera into the file
  --up-axis AXIS     y | z (default y)
  --left-handed      the scene is left-handed
  --unit-scale N     units per metre in the target
  --json             result as one JSON document on stdout

The camera is not solved here.  `solve` recovers it by inverting the run's
view-projection and records it in the manifest; this stage carries it into
the file, in the scene's frame, with the field of view the projection
implies.
help.inspect:
rdc2blendCppCli inspect PATH [options]

Reads the files this tool produces and reports what is in them: a
draw dump (inputs.bin) or a mesh (.mesh2 / .world2).  PATH may be a
file or a directory; a directory is searched for both.  Exit code 1
means at least one file could not be read, and each failure says why.

  --file-list FILE   read the paths from a file, one per line
  --path FILE        the same as a positional path; here for a caller
                     that builds its arguments as a list
  --expected FILE    compare against a recorded JSON document
  --tolerance N      how close is close enough for --expected
  --verbose         one line per file, and per-file detail
  --json            the full result as one JSON document
help.matrices:
rdc2blendCppCli matrices [options]

Prints the frame and scene matrices a run would use - the transform from
the capture's world into the target's.  Reads no file: it reports what
the settings below imply, which is what makes it useful for seeing the
effect of changing one, and it also reports whether the frame is
orthogonal (conjugated transforms depend on that) and whether the scene
transform is affine.

  --up-axis AXIS     y | z (default y)
  --left-handed      the frame is left-handed
  --unit-scale N     units per metre in the target (default 1)
  --offset-x N       scene offset, metres (default 0)
  --offset-y N       the same for Y
  --offset-z N       the same for Z
  --expected FILE    compare against a recorded JSON document
  --tolerance N      how close is close enough for --expected
  --json             the matrices as one JSON document on stdout

Exit code 2 means the settings are not usable: a frame that is not
orthogonal, or a scene matrix that is not affine.
help.parse:
rdc2blendCppCli parse [DIR] [options]

Reads a work directory's raw dump and works out what is in it: which
draws are skinned, where each one's bone palette is, which constant
buffer holds the view-projection, and where the camera sits.  Writes its
result beside the dump and changes nothing in raw/.  DIR is the
directory `read` wrote; it defaults to <workspace>/imi/<task>/read.

  --raw DIR          the directory `read` wrote
  --solver NAME      the engine's rules, by pack name or path to a
                     solver.json.  REQUIRED: this tool ships no game's
                     rules, so with nothing named there is nothing to read
                     the capture with.  `doctor` lists what is installed
  --group-by FIELDS  what a pass is keyed by (default: depth,viewport)
  --eid N            only this event id
  --palette-base SPEC  where the palette is, as SLOT|NAME:INDEX:COMPONENT.
                     Repeatable and comma-separated: the list is the
                     point, because a profile may declare two locations
                     and one flag cannot pair an index with a component
  --palette-cb N     the constant buffer slot holding the palette
  --palette-cb-name NAME  the same, by block name
  --palette-index N  the index inside that buffer
  --palette-component C  which component of a matrix array is the palette
  --palette-header-offset N  bytes before the first bone
  --expected FILE    compare the result against a recorded JSON document
  --tolerance N      how close is close enough for --expected
  --json             result as one JSON document on stdout

The three older palette flags select ONE location.  Giving them spends
half the candidates and says so; prefer --palette-base.
help.read:
rdc2blendCppCli read --capture FILE [options]

Opens a .rdc and dumps what the pipeline needs into one directory: raw/
holds the draw dump and the constant buffers, and survey.json sits beside
it.  This is the only stage that needs RenderDoc, and the only one not
written in C++ - it runs a Python driver inside a head-less qrenderdoc,
so the first thing to check when it fails is `doctor`'s driver line.

  --capture FILE     the .rdc (required)
  --work DIR         where to write (default <workspace>/imi/<task>/read)
  --qrenderdoc EXE   the qrenderdoc to run (default: PATH, then Program
                     Files)
  --driver FILE      the driver script (default <root>/env/rdc_driver.py)
  --package-root DIR where the driver's Python package lives
  --package-name NAME  the package the driver imports
                     (default rdc2blend_env)
  --read-stage NAME  all | survey | dumps - how far to go (default all)
  --solver NAME      the rules the driver reads the capture with
  --pad N            alignment for dumped blocks (default 1024)
  --max-draws N      stop after this many draws (default 8000)
  --min-bone-bytes N a dump at least this large is taken for a palette
                     (default 262144)
  --no-mesh          do not dump mesh data
  --no-depth         do not dump depth
  --textures         dump textures as well
  --read-timeout SEC give up after this long (default 3600)
  --json             result as one JSON document on stdout
help.run:
rdc2blendCppCli run --capture FILE [options]

Runs the pipeline, stopping after --stage.  With no --stage it runs
every stage whose artifacts are not already complete, so re-running
a finished task does nothing and an interrupted one continues.

  --capture FILE     the .rdc (required)
  --task NAME        task name; default is the capture's file name
  --task-root DIR    the task's directory, if it is not the usual one
  --stage NAME       read | parse | solve | emit
  --from NAME        start at this stage even if earlier ones are done
  --component ID     component id or game name
  --tag TAG          lts | beta | alpha | dev
  --force            redo the stage even when it is already complete
  --dry-run          say what would run, and change nothing
  --config FILE      JSON merged over the defaults
  --set K=V          one config key, repeatable (dotted keys nest)
  --origin WHERE     world | character: what the scene's origin is
  --no-camera        do not carry the recovered camera into the scene
  --json             result as one JSON document on stdout
help.selftest:
rdc2blendCppCli selftest [options]

Runs the built-in checks.  Needs no capture, no RenderDoc, no Blender and
no GPU, and writes nothing outside a temporary directory - it is the
check that a build works at all, and the one thing to run after changing
anything in the core library.

  --verbose          name every check as it passes, not just the count
  --json             one document with every check's name and result

Exit code 1 means at least one check failed; the failing names are on
stderr, with the value that was expected and the value that was got.
help.solve:
rdc2blendCppCli solve [DIR] [options]

Picks each draw's bone palette and fits the transform that puts it where
the capture had it, then writes the meshes and a manifest into world2/.
Reads the dump `read` wrote; DIR defaults to <workspace>/imi/<task>/read.

  --raw DIR          the directory `read` wrote
  --solver NAME      the engine's rules, by pack name or path to a
                     solver.json.  REQUIRED: a wrong palette still fits a
                     pose, so an unnamed one is refused rather than
                     guessed.  `doctor` lists what is installed
  --limit N          solve at most this many draws (0 = all)
  --eid N            only this event id
  --emit-mesh DIR    write the solved meshes here (the camera is solved
                     with them, which is why this is not a plain dump)
  --manifest FILE    write the manifest here
  --palette-header-offset N  bytes before the first bone
  --bone-stride-f4 N how many float4 one bone takes
  --max-align-delta N  the largest residual still called a match
  --trace-placement  say why each draw was placed where it was
  --normals NAME     auto | game | computed - where a vertex stream that
                     carries no usable normal gets one
  --vp-cb N          the constant buffer holding the view-projection
  --vp-cb-name NAME  the same, by block name
  --vp-rows LIST     which of its rows, as float4 indices
  --vp-row-major     read those rows row-major
  --placement-tolerance N  how far off a placement may be, in 1e-10
                     units; 0 disables the check
  --expected FILE    compare the result against a recorded JSON document
  --tolerance N      how close is close enough for --expected
  --json             result as one JSON document on stdout
help.status:
rdc2blendCppCli status --task NAME [options]

Reads <task>/handoff.json and reports each stage's state and whether
its artifacts are still on disk.  Changes nothing.

  --task NAME       the task to report on
  --task-root DIR   report on a task directory directly
  --json            result as one JSON document on stdout
help.usage:
rdc2blendCpp - recover assets from a RenderDoc capture.

  rdc2blendCppCli <command> [options]

Commands:
  doctor        check the environment and report what was found
  components    list the component modules that can be loaded
  status        read a task's handoff and say where it got to
  run           run one stage of a task, or the whole pipeline
  read          read a .rdc into a work directory, by running
                qrenderdoc head-less (the only stage that needs it)
  inspect       read a draw dump or mesh file and report its contents
  matrices      print the frame and scene matrices (where the world sits)
  parse         read the capture description and report the matrices
  solve         pick each draw's palette and fit its transform
  emit-fbx      write each solved part out as a binary FBX
  emit-scene    write the neutral description file a DCC reads
  selftest      run the built-in checks; needs no capture, no
                RenderDoc, no Blender and no GPU

Common options:
  --workspace DIR   the workspace root (default: found by walking up
                    from the executable, looking for imi/ and tmp/)
  --capture FILE    the .rdc to work from
  --task NAME       the task name (default: the capture's file name)
  --component ID    which component to use, by id or game name.  Optional:
                    with no component at all the host runs every stage
                    itself, and only `--solver` is then required
  --solver NAME     the engine's rules, by pack name or by path to a
                    solver.json.  REQUIRED by any stage that reads a
                    capture's constants: this tool ships no game's rules
                    of its own, and reading one game's capture with
                    another's rules gives a wrong answer rather than an
                    error.  `doctor` lists the packs that are installed
  --tag TAG         prefer lts / beta / alpha / dev when picking
  --stage NAME      run just this stage, or up to and including it
  --config FILE     a JSON file merged over the defaults
  --set K=V         set one config key, repeatable
  --json            write the result as one JSON document on stdout
  --help            this text.  Every command below also prints its own
                    options - `<command> --help` - and that block, not
                    this list, is that command's contract.
                    Note `emit-scene --geometry-ext` names the GEOMETRY
                    files' extension while `--ext` names the description
                    file's - passing the wrong one is not an error, it
                    just points at files that are not there.
